sectionHeading: The Corporation: Coordinating Exchange at Velocity
authority: Editorial craft owned by the editorial agent under author delegation. Historical claim scope remains an author decision.

ledgerSearch.outcome: No recorded decision touches this section. CTD-0013 concerns the corpus claim about historical extraction as a moral claim and is an open obligation rather than a ruling; the restored logic of externalized cost is consistent with it and is recorded there. The world population figure of eight billion is restored as written and is current within rounding.

findings.summary: The section's sharpest argument was deleted.

evidence.baseline: The deeper problem is that the corporation has colonized not just the economy but the imagination. We now reflexively reach for corporate structures when we want to build anything at scale, even when what we are trying to build is precisely the thing that corporate logic destroys.

findings.diagnosis: This is the only paragraph in the chapter that turns the survey on the reader and on the project. It explains why a book proposing a new institution must argue against a default rather than merely against a competitor, and it is the premise of the later chapter on why Providence must not be a startup. Removing it leaves that later chapter without its ground.

findings.summary: The concrete achievements and the concrete unpriceable things were both generalized.

evidence.baseline: It built the railroads, electrified the cities, produced the vaccines, and created the supply chains that feed and clothe the world's eight billion people. ... a functioning atmosphere, a living river, a community's coherence, a future generation's inheritance.
evidence.shipped: It has built infrastructure, produced medicines, organized supply chains ... A living river, a community's trust, and a stable atmosphere resist pricing.

findings.diagnosis: Railroads became infrastructure, vaccines became medicines, and eight billion people disappeared. The volume card asks that every sustained abstraction return to a body, relationship, rule, resource, place, or observable consequence. These four verbs are that return, and they are also what makes the paragraph a genuine credit rather than a concession. The unpriceable list lost a future generation's inheritance, which is the one item that connects this section to the volume's dedication.

evidence.baseline: The corporation's fundamental logic fenced around a three-verb definition, and but the imagination.

findings.diagnosis: The first fenced a three-part definition inside a subject that then took a colon of its own; the sentence was split so the definition stands alone and the incapacity claim follows with its colon intact. The second introduced a consequence and became a period, so the reflex it describes lands as its own sentence.

debtImpact.note: Perhaps the most efficient coordination mechanism ever created returns. The hedge perhaps is in the baseline and is preserved.
The restored externalization argument states the moral claim about cost-shifting in structural rather than accusatory terms, which is the direction the item asks for.

openQuestions: Heading. Coordinating Exchange at Velocity keeps the section parallel with the other five and names the function. Action at Speed names a quality. Not changed. Renaming costs a section id and a recorded route alias in publishing/continuity.

regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. F2 records the generalization habit at its clearest: four verbs with objects became four verbs with categories, and the paragraph lost both its evidence and its willingness to credit the institution it is about to criticize.
